preamble: ESCAPE | I’m taking my daughter, aged 11, to New York early next year and was planning to go business class. I have not decided which airline to use, but a friend mentioned that some did not like taking children in business. Are there any restrictions on age? Stephanie Jones, St Albans, Herts None of the major transatlantic carriers has lower age restrictions in their premium cabins. I took a sample from a selection of some of the many airlines ß ying this route. British Airways and Virgin Atlantic offer a 25 per cent discount for under-12s and have ß at beds in Club World and Upper Class respectively. For a six-day trip in February over a long weekend, BA.com quoted £2,061 for an adult, £1,585 for children under 12. Virgin (www.virginatlantic.com ) was more expensive at £2,146/£1,645. Both have excellent facilities for children and also offer premium economy, which you may wish to consider at least one way if you’re taking a day ß ight and will have less need for a ß at bed. MaxJet (www.maxjet.com ) and Silver Jet (www.silverjet.co.uk ), ß ying to New York business-class only from Stansted and Luton, were competitively priced on the dates we tried at £1,032 and £799 per person, but don’t offer child discounts. We plan to visit North Yorkshire early next year for a long weekend. Our Þrst stop will be Whitby . Can you recommend some attractive places to stay in the area or tell us of a decent website that can do the job for us? Ian Roebuck, by email
